/usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/terminal-review112-terminal-mock-check-046e04aaae45.py control "$HOME/mock-control.jsonl" || exit 96
/usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/system-sequence.py --notify kill --reply kill=ESRCH --log-args kill=0,1 --notify getpriority --reply getpriority=15 --log-args getpriority=0,1 --notify setpriority --reply setpriority=0 --log-args setpriority=0,1,2 --errno tkill:EPERM --errno tgkill:EPERM --log "$HOME/mock-esrch.jsonl" -- /usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/terminal-review112-terminal-mock-check-046e04aaae45.py probe-esrch > "$HOME/mock-esrch.out" || exit 97
/usr/bin/python3 /opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/terminal-review112-terminal-mock-check-046e04aaae45.py control-esrch "$HOME/mock-esrch.jsonl" || exit 98

cases.oracle: The original no-mutation obligation: seccomp user notification intercepts every kill/getpriority/setpriority and replies synthetically without forwarding. The fixed PID is above Linux pid_max; setup independently calls the intercepted syscalls and verifies exact replies/arguments before target behavior.
cases.comparison: Prompt/validation or result screen, followed by exact recorded syscall names, args and synthetic reply; no actual signal or priority change. Raw terminal and seccomp logs are retained.
